method: GET official MITRE XML; direct web pages previously timed out

1336.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine
1336.description: The product uses a template engine to insert or process externally-influenced input, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements or syntax that can be interpreted as template expressions or other code directives when processed by the engine.

20.name: Improper Input Validation
20.description:
The product receives input or data, but it does
        not validate or incorrectly validates that the input has the
        properties that are required to process the data safely and
        correctly.

200.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
200.description: The product exposes sensitive information to an actor that is not explicitly authorized to have access to that information.

209.name: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information
209.description: The product generates an error message that includes sensitive information about its environment, users, or associated data.

22.name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
22.description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that is intended to identify a file or directory that is located underneath a restricted parent directory, but the product does not properly neutralize special elements within the pathname that can cause the pathname to resolve to a location that is outside of the restricted directory.

269.name: Improper Privilege Management
269.description: The product does not properly assign, modify, track, or check privileges for an actor, creating an unintended sphere of control for that actor.

287.name: Improper Authentication
287.description: When an actor claims to have a given identity, the product does not prove or insufficiently proves that the claim is correct.

294.name: Authentication Bypass by Capture-replay
294.description: A capture-replay flaw exists when the design of the product makes it possible for a malicious user to sniff network traffic and bypass authentication by replaying it to the server in question to the same effect as the original message (or with minor changes).

307.name: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts
307.description: The product does not implement sufficient measures to prevent multiple failed authentication attempts within a short time frame.

345.name: Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity
345.description: The product does not sufficiently verify the origin or authenticity of data, in a way that causes it to accept invalid data.

362.name: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition')
362.description: The product contains a concurrent code sequence that requires temporary, exclusive access to a shared resource, but a timing window exists in which the shared resource can be modified by another code sequence operating concurrently.

384.name: Session Fixation
384.description: Authenticating a user, or otherwise establishing a new user session, without invalidating any existing session identifier gives an attacker the opportunity to steal authenticated sessions.

400.name: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
400.description: The product does not properly control the allocation and maintenance of a limited resource.

434.name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
434.description: The product allows the upload or transfer of dangerous file types that are automatically processed within its environment.

502.name: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
502.description: The product deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently ensuring that the resulting data will be valid.

611.name: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference
611.description: The product processes an XML document that can contain XML entities with URIs that resolve to documents outside of the intended sphere of control, causing the product to embed incorrect documents into its output.

639.name: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
639.description: The system's authorization functionality does not prevent one user from gaining access to another user's data or record by modifying the key value identifying the data.

640.name: Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password
640.description: The product contains a mechanism for users to recover or change their passwords without knowing the original password, but the mechanism is weak.

78.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
78.description: The product constructs all or part of an OS command using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the intended OS command when it is sent to a downstream component.

79.name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
79.description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output that is used as a web page that is served to other users.

862.name: Missing Authorization
862.description: The product does not perform an authorization check when an actor attempts to access a resource or perform an action.

89.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
89.description: The product constructs all or part of an SQL command using externally-influenced input from an upstream component, but it does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes special elements that could modify the intended SQL command when it is sent to a downstream component. Without sufficient removal or quoting of SQL syntax in user-controllable inputs, the generated SQL query can cause those inputs to be interpreted as SQL instead of ordinary user data.

915.name: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes
915.description: The product receives input from an upstream component that specifies multiple attributes, properties, or fields that are to be initialized or updated in an object, but it does not properly control which attributes can be modified.

916.name: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort
916.description: The product generates a hash for a password, but it uses a scheme that does not provide a sufficient level of computational effort that would make password cracking attacks infeasible or expensive.

918.name: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
918.description: The web server receives a URL or similar request from an upstream component and retrieves the contents of this URL, but it does not sufficiently ensure that the request is being sent to the expected destination.
